elements.evidence: The rendered Section 9.0(f) retains a solicitation restriction binding on both parties ("Neither party will ... in any way solicit for employment any of the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement"). Customer (IBM), which was the only restricted party in the original, remains restricted, so the preferred no-restriction outcome is not achieved.

"Neither party will ... solicit for employment any of the other party's personnel ... without the prior written consent of the other party" — the one-sided "IBM agrees that ... it will not" formulation and the MSL-only consent right are replaced with reciprocal wording, and the carve-outs are conformed to "that party"/"such party".

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Covered population is narrowed from "any Transferred Employees" to "any of the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement"; the dangling "such Transferred Employees" in the search-firm proviso is conformed to "such personnel". In this outsourcing agreement the Services are the work performed under the Agreement, so "directly involved in performing this Agreement" tracks the element.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of an individual's involvement in performing this Agreement" replaces "for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date"; both the length (12 months) and the temporal anchor (end of involvement) match the element.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained and conformed limb (b): "by using general solicitation or general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto" — general advertising is expressly excluded (the original "general employment advertising or communications" already covered this).

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained and conformed limb (a): "employing any such person who contacts that party on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from that party".

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is solicitation only — "in any way solicit for employment" — and both carve-outs expressly permit "employing"/"hiring" the person; no "employ or engage" or no-hire language is introduced or retained.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the rendered clause is mutual, scoped to personnel directly involved in performing the Agreement, capped at 12 months from the end of that involvement, retains the unsolicited-approach and general-advertising carve-outs, and prohibits solicitation only (no no-hire). Position-complete at the fallback level.

Preferred level is not met and cannot be, because the redline retains a restriction binding Customer (IBM). That is an acceptable choice given the finding targets the fallback, but the comment should make clear to the client that Customer remains restricted where it previously was the only restricted party.

Edits are confined to the four items the fallback requires (mutuality, scope, duration/anchor, conforming the carve-outs and the now-dangling "such Transferred Employees" reference). No survival tail, expense, procedure or extra obligation is added, and the favourable existing search-firm proviso and consent mechanic are retained.

Minor trim available without affecting completeness: the inserted words "general solicitation or" are not strictly necessary, since the retained "general employment advertising or communications" already satisfied the general-advertisement element. Treated as de minimis conforming language rather than a minimality failure, but the drafter could delete it to keep the redline tightest.

Intent preserved: no undefined term or dangling cross-reference results — "Transferred Employees" remains defined elsewhere and is simply no longer used in this clause, consent is reciprocated to "the other party", and no other allocation, timing or commercial mechanic in Section 9.0 is contradicted.

Note on scope re-cut (correctly flagged in the rationale): moving from "Transferred Employees" to "personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement" narrows in some respects and broadens in others (e.g., Vendor personnel never transferred are now covered against Customer solicitation). This tracks the playbook fallback, so it is not a defect, but confirm the client accepts the re-cut.
